description: Wide-net raw GPU price snapshotting (capture ONLY -- this lane computes nothing, but since the 2026-08-23 hourly panel mint its stored record IS consumed, read-only, by the six panel-index calc lanes (METHODOLOGY.md), so a collector/recipe change here CAN move a contractual panel print: treat collector edits with basket-lane care. No lane ever writes under this keyspace; the panel loader refuses such a prefix mechanically). The original point stands: historical accumulation -- capture gaps can never be backfilled, so the record started before any methodology existed. Fully separate from the basket lanes (index/b300_basket, index/b200_basket) — shared transport/slot/store machinery, disjoint keyspace, own schedule. Collectors record EVERY GPU rental price row their surface publishes that the recipe can pin — all chips, all vendors, all tiers, labeled — with canonical skus derived by the framework from config/gpu_sku_catalog.json (unmapped labels recorded honestly, never guessed). Every parameter here is operational config, not code. min_sources_to_claim is deliberately LOW relative to the source count: a thin snapshot is still raw history AND still an honest panel input (the panel lanes screen per member and publish explicit dark artifacts on thin hours -- a recorded thin hour beats a lost one), so the gate only refuses catastrophically broken captures; scraper rot on a wide net is expected and shows up as per-source error holes, not lost days.

sources.notes: JSON-LD offers on /pricing — all GPU rows, all tiers (on-demand, spot, serverless continuous/spot, instant-cluster) with the name-suffix <-> description double-read tier pin; leading 'Nx ' count is the only per-GPU divisor (rows without one are skipped, never assumed 1x); storage offers excluded by their own description (out of scope, silent); blank-model CPU rows and disagreeing-currency-label rows skipped into partial_errors.

Server-rendered price table (escaped JSON) — all GPU rows, on-demand + preemptible columns; exact-header + exactly-once table pins; unpriced NVL72 contact-us rows counted in partial_errors; 'from $' floors keep the qualifier in raw_value + extra.

gpu-pricing page — all three tables, tiers labeled: On-Demand GPU Pricing (spec-column fence), Reservation Pricing 'Starting from' floors (Reserve-here fence, tier reserved), Spot VM Pricing (section slice, tier spot).
Public unauthenticated instance-catalog API — every GPU instance type in the catalog; bills EUR, recorded natively (price_usd_gpu_hr stays null).
GraphQL gpuTypes — every listed GPU; secure AND community cloud, on-demand AND spot, recorded as separate labeled observations (the basket lane records secure on-demand only).

bundles API, per-chip queries from options.gpu_names (grow the list = config edit; gpu_name is an exact-case string match — copy vast's own spellings verbatim, e.g. 'RTX 6000Ada' with no space, 'RTX PRO 6000 WS'/'RTX PRO 6000 S' because bare 'RTX PRO 6000' returns zero). Records the cheapest machines per chip (dedup by machine, ranked per-GPU) up to record_limit_per_gpu, with book_stats accounting for what was left out. Chips in population_gpu_names (must be a subset of gpu_names, validated fail-closed) ALSO record every verified-US/CA machine beyond the cheapest-N, marked book_scope=verified_us_ca_population and capped at 200 with an explicit overflow flag: the full population the hourly panels' verified-US/CA statistics run over (the truncated-book capture fix ported config-driven; screen imported from gpu_index.index.composite, one home). 'MI300X' returns zero offers today — kept deliberately as a tripwire for AMD capacity appearing (costs one call, records an honest empty-book partial note). Big consumer-card books (>= 100 offers) emit persistent 'book wider than both fetch windows' partial notes — honest coverage accounting, not a fault.
Next.js RSC flight rows on /pricing — every GPU VM row with a real price cell (generic row-key regex, price window bounded at the next row key of any sku).

Bare-metal plan blobs — every GPU plan, hourly + monthly-commit tiers labeled, per-region with stock_level in extra. Bills USD + BRL (separately-set list prices, not FX) — BRL recorded natively with price_usd_gpu_hr null; the catalog plausibility bands screen USD prints only, so BRL rows are recorded unscreened.

USD pricing table — every GPU row, hourly + monthly-commit + annual (reserved) tiers, per-row ~730x/~10.5x cross-checks; plus the page's JSON-LD offer catalog (same GPUs' INR hourly list prices, recorded natively).
Homepage JSON blobs re-publishing other clouds' capacity — every GPU type; first_party false, cloud attribution in extra is the load-bearing disclosure.
Instances-pricing table — every data-plan row (all chips, all tab sizes), on-demand instance rates; committed 1-Click Cluster tiers recorded separately labeled where pinnable.
On-demand GPU instance table, both regions — every row segment (incl. GB200/GB300 rack-scale parts, first-class skus here), labeled On-Demand + Spot Price spans only.

GPU Clusters combined table — every hardware row: ON-Demand column plus the reserved tenor columns (tier reserved, tenor in extra); em-dash cells skipped silently, 'Contact us' cells counted in partial_errors; Dedicated Inference section excluded by slice.

Public no-auth /api/listings, per-chip queries from options.gpus (2-page cap per slug; the h100/a100 books exceed it — the cheapest ~400 are recorded with a loud partial note). LEADS, NOT PRINTS: rows are mostly verification_level 0 / human_verified false — recorded with that metadata intact in extra so consumers can screen; first_party false. amd-mi325x is a genuinely empty book today, kept as a watch slot.

Public no-auth /api/supply?intent=selling&include_ended=false -- seller-declared capacity-offer classifieds republished by the aggregator (meta.notice verbatim: discovery records, not guaranteed quotes; sellers can be Anonymous). The availability window IS the payload: available_now / availability_state / available_from / available_until plus min_bookable_gpus / min_duration_hours / interconnect ride verbatim in extra. No billing_type on this surface -- tier is DERIVED by ruling (min_duration_hours >= 720 -> monthly-commit, else on-demand) with the derivation recorded per row. Unpriced offers (price null = not stated; a real Anonymous 8x H100 row exists) are counted in book_stats (offers_unpriced / offers_available_now), never $0 rows. Whole selling book fits one page today (25 offers live 2026-08-25); no sort param -- supply 400s on the listings sort enum.

Server-rendered MUI table on /pricing ('Custom LLMs' dedicated-GPU section; header exactly GPU|Memory|Price is the identity pin, price cells must fullmatch '$X / GPU-hour', duplicated header-matching tables must agree) — A100/H100/H200/B200/B300 USD per GPU-hour, dedicated custom-model deployment tier (pay-for-uptime container hosting, minute-granularity billing, not a bare VM). Serverless per-token tables and tier-multiplier tables on the same page are excluded by the header pin; B200/B300 clusters are contact-only with no price rows.

Public no-auth cetools price-list JSON (apexapps.oracle.com /pls/apex/cetools/api/v1/products/?currencyCode=USD, trailing slash load-bearing) — the same backend that hydrates oracle.com/cloud/compute/pricing. Single GET (~189KB). Fence metricName == 'GPU Per Hour' exactly, pin rows by partNumber (stable SKU anchor with a name-drift tripwire), take the PAY_AS_YOU_GO USD value. Excludes 'NVIDIA AI Enterprise' software-license lookalikes and Compute Cloud@Customer appliance rows (counted in book_stats); all fencing is client-side (server ignores name/serviceCategory filters). Legacy shape names that don't name a chip (GPU Standard X7/V2, GPU E3/E4) stay honestly unmapped.

Server-rendered /pricing GPU tables (section#nvidia-gpus fence, caption-pinned per chip, 'N x NVIDIA ...' product-detail row pin) — per-instance USD hourly divided by the row's pinned GPU count; on-demand + 6/12/24/36-month commitment terms recorded as separate labeled observations (tier reserved, commitment_months in extra; B200 is commitment-only by design, never zero-filled).

Server-rendered /en/pricing GPU cards — h3 'NVIDIA <chip>' paired with adjacent 'from $X.XX' + '/GPU-hour' spans; USD from-floor list prices (page FAQ: on-demand vs committed differ, so tier recorded as from_floor, never on-demand). Unpriced pre-order cards skipped with a partial_error; GB200/GB300 map to their own skus, never B200/B300. The fetch sends the project User-Agent (gpu_index.common.http); the /en/ locale URL is pinned.

Docs pricing page (server-rendered) — On-Demand + Spot GPU Droplet tables sliced by h2 anchor ids; 1x per-GPU rows and (8x) full-droplet rows recorded as separate labeled observations (whole-droplet price + gpu_count_basis from the page's own (Nx) label). Contract table is unpriced by design and excluded. B300 exists only in the spot tier (public preview). The fetch sends the project User-Agent (gpu_index.common.http).

Serverless & Compute Pricing table on /pricing (server-rendered; fail-closed header pin GPU|VRAM|List Price|As low as, exactly one matching table) — USD per GPU-hour for fal's own serverless fleet; List Price recorded tier=serverless and the 'As low as' column as a separate labeled contact-sales floor (serverless_as_low_as), never as the list rate; per-output model-API tables excluded by the header pin.

Server-rendered Astro pricing cards on /pricing — MI300X only today: VM on-demand $/GPU/hr (per-minute billing, new-customer rate) + 8x bare-metal one-month-minimum rate labeled monthly-commit; grandfathered existing-customer rate recorded tier legacy while published. One of few AMD principals. The fetch sends the project User-Agent (gpu_index.common.http). Unpriced parts (MI355X) never get invented rows.

Homepage #pricing live-offers table (Next.js ISR ~5min; render timestamp in extra) — live on-demand USD 'From / GPU / hr' FLOOR prices. Pins: unique id=pricing anchor + byte-exact thead + the literal table-footer marker naming LIVE OFFERS / CLOUD.SESTERCE.COM / USD / ON-DEMAND (middle-dot separated on the page; currency+tier pin, fails closed if USD or ON-DEMAND drops out). Rows parse from the single pinned tbody only (marquee duplicates and the stale CLI-demo capacity strip are skipped + counted).

Public /compute marketplace page server-renders the full /gpu-cloud/instances/offers book into its Next.js RSC flight payload (read anonymously, no JS; cache-control no-store, fresh per request). Join-then-scan of self.__next_f.push chunks; fail-closed pins: exactly one "filteredOffers":[ page-wide (RSC reference strings never match), balanced-bracket slice, json.loads-or-raise, $undefined-inside-slice raises. One observation per offer: sku_identifier = raw gpuName, per-GPU = instance-total hourlyPrice / gpuCount (float artifacts kept in raw_value); verbatim per-region availability booleans + instance_id/deployment_type/cloud_name (anonymized upstream tag) in extra; gpuCount<1 CPU tiers and zero prices skipped + counted; standing partial_error names homepage-advertised chips (B200/B300) absent from the book; book_stats records the offer count per capture (server-side default-filter tripwire). Sibling of sesterce -- the homepage floor table runs on its own ISR clock and the two surfaces are never reconciled at collect time.

Server-rendered /pricing comparison grid, TensorPool column ONLY (double pin: exact header order + the highlight class on exactly the TensorPool cell of every row; competitor columns share the same chip labels and are never recorded). On-demand USD per GPU-hour; CPU/storage rows fenced out; the mobile-card rendering is an equality tripwire, never a second set of rows.

Public no-auth /api/executors JSON — the whole live machine book in one response; price_per_gpu = USD/GPU/hr (basis proven by the UI toggle), tier secure|spot mapped fail-closed to on-demand|spot, dedup by machine id, miner/validator hotkeys retained as attribution in extra. pending_price_per_hour + effective-date ride in extra as a SCHEDULED change, never recorded as current.

Public no-auth JSON API: GET https://api.gpu.ai/v1/pricing?limit=200, follow next_cursor (hard cap 10 pages) — every offer row (gpu_type x gpu_count x region x capacity_class), on-demand + spot. price_per_hour covers the WHOLE configuration: per-GPU = price_per_hour / gpu_count. No currency field — USD pinned from the provider's own dollar prints; a future row-level currency key != USD refuses. secure AND community capacity classes recorded separately; offering_id is the stable per-offer identity. Never collect from the /gpus or /pricing HTML pages (static/client-fetched).

Server-rendered Webflow pricing page — 'GPU instances pricing' table, On-demand + Current spot columns (spot recorded only when numeric). Row fence = exact '$D.DD/GPU-hr' suffix inside the GPU-instances section (excludes CPU $/vCPU-hr rows, the Serverless Inference $/M-token table, and Self-Serve Deployments rows with identical chip headings). A100 SXM/PCIe disambiguated by form-factor tag; unpriced contact-sales rows (GB200/B200/MI355X) admitted automatically if numbers ever publish.

Public no-auth order-catalog JSON, two billing subsidiaries recorded natively (FR bills EUR, full lineup; separate US entity bills USD). Rows pinned by blobs.commercial.brick=='gpu' + blobs.technical.gpu model/number (per-GPU divisor); price ints are 1e-8 currency units cross-checked per row against the cent-rounded formattedPrice, ex-VAT; tier from planCode suffix (.consumption = hourly on-demand, .monthly.postpaid = monthly-commit at 730h/month), NEVER intervalUnit (US publishes 'none' on both). Windows-license and legacy variants recorded labeled. FR body is ~97% of the 8MiB transport cap — a growth alarm rides in partial_errors on every capture.

Unauthenticated dashboard API GET https://cloud-api.voltagepark.com/api/v1/bare-metal/locations (the SPA's logged-out variant) — rows keyed by specs_per_node.gpu_model with gpu_price_ethernet + gpu_price_infiniband as decimal strings, USD per GPU/hr; recorded as two on-demand observations distinguished by extra.network (networking variants, NOT an on-demand/reserved split). Availability counts can be 0 while prices stay published (metadata, never a gate); no currency field (USD pinned from provider dollar prints); fails closed on missing/renamed fields or pagination appearing.

Public no-auth /v2/alpha/on-demand/rental-options JSON — every on-demand option; costPerHourCents is the whole-option total, divided by required gpuCount (never defaulted) for per-GPU USD; missing totalAvailable stays unknown and availability never gates price; providerCostPerHourCents is deliberately never republished; unknown *PerHourCents keys fail closed.
